purpose: The complete Part B disposition for every original certified blocker and every AUDIT-F item, per the phase's own required taxonomy (CERTIFIED_CLOSED / CERTIFIED_SCOPE_RESOLVED / STILL_OPEN / NEW_COUPLED_BLOCKER_DISCOVERED per blocker; CERTIFIED_CLOSED / STILL_OPEN per AUDIT-F item).

blockerDispositions.title: Structural heading/rank-stack corruption
blockerDispositions.summary: Both Part A fixes (page-number whitespace preservation, unionMatches) held under fresh attack; all real-fixture sites and DSGR spans reconfirmed. But 4 new, general, reproducible false-negative defects found: (1) lowercase section/article keyword not at line-start is invisible (missing case-insensitive flag on shape-based patterns); (2) a footnote-marker digit glued to terminal punctuation with only one newline before the next heading drops the heading, demonstrably re-parenting a real child SECTION to parentSectionRef:null (real rank-stack corruption); (3) multi-column-layout collapse can drop a heading and merge content into the wrong section's span; (4) RX's own widened page-number-artifact regex does not recognize the ALL-CAPS 'PAGE' running-footer convention it claims to cover.

blockerDispositions.title: Supersession signal lost before DiscoveredCandidate
blockerDispositions.summary: End-to-end proof with real Postgres: a genuine amendment supersedes a provision; the resulting DiscoveredCandidate.supersessionStatus is genuinely KNOWN_SUPERSEDED, the persisted SemanticTruthRecord.operativeLineage.operativeStatus is genuinely OPERATIVE_STATE_CONFLICTED, and sufficiency is CONFLICTED (not COMPLETE) even when the compiler adversarially asserted COMPLETE - proving normalize.ts's enforceSufficiencyConsistency genuinely overrides the compiler end-to-end in the live orchestrator. Worst-first multi-node attack also held.

blockerDispositions.title: Null operativeState failing open
blockerDispositions.summary: A standalone never-amended document correctly does not falsely downgrade; the EMPTY_SUPERSESSION_INDEX fail-closed branch is confirmed correct by construction.

blockerDispositions.title: LLM-facing tools bypassing operative state
blockerDispositions.summary: New real defect: lib/contract-model/compiler/semantic/tools.ts's getDefinition tool silently serves raw, stale definition text with a plain source:"base-document" label - indistinguishable from a never-amended term - when a term has a real, on-file AMBIGUOUS/PARTIAL amendment record. Its sibling getOperativeProvision correctly discloses status in every branch; getDefinition does not in any branch. Live-wired (used by the real semantic compiler), reproduced with a direct test.

blockerDispositions.title: Ambiguous DEFINITION amendment reaching false verified state
blockerDispositions.summary: BLOCKER-6's own cross-reference-audit mechanism is correct in isolation, but the BLOCKER-5 getDefinition defect provides a coupled, unguarded pathway to the exact harm BLOCKER-6 exists to prevent (an ambiguous DEFINITION amendment reaching a semantic compiler as if fully resolved).

blockerDispositions.title: Persisted ContractRule source-trace defect / unbackfilled rows
blockerDispositions.summary: Idempotency at rest confirmed (0/71 affected on fresh dry-run). Independent resolution-count re-derivation (two separate fresh query methods) matches 106/191 and 73/95 exactly. 4 new adversarial cases (null documentId schema-unreachability, same-term-different-document non-merge, fresh real-Postgres collision handling, cross-tenant isolation) all held.

blockerDispositions.title: Sibling claim identity collision
blockerDispositions.summary: All 9 of Workstream D's original cases, plus fresh attacks (different value types, dates never mistaken for anchors, hallucinated-number rejection, paraphrase-hash rejection, version-bump cache-key correctness) held. But a genuine new defect found: findCoordinateClauseSplit performs at most ONE split per region and never recurses - a sentence fusing THREE independently-operative claims with distinct numbers only partially separates (claims 2 and 3 collapse into one semanticUnitId). Falsifies the 'unconditional, always-active closure' framing; squarely inside AUDIT-F4's own frozen defect class.

blockerDispositions.title: Independent verifier missing omitted qualifying condition
blockerDispositions.summary: isSynthetic gating, verifier independence, and the original 7-case reproduction all held. But 8 of 12 new real-world condition phrasings ('upon the occurrence of,' 'as and when'+'following,' passive 'shall be deemed satisfied when,' a bare defined-term-only trigger, a schedule-cross-reference-only condition, non-numeric 'in the event of'/'in the event that'/'to the extent that') are NOT detected by source-inventory.ts's CONDITIONAL_PHRASE list, reproducing BLOCKER-9's exact original failure mode with new vocabulary - the third occurrence of this same defect class across three consecutive phases (3F.1.6.R, then 3F.1.6.RX Part A, now found again in Part B).

blockerDispositions.title: Contract-model pipeline not a complete, durable live application trust path
blockerDispositions.summary: Umbrella blocker; STILL_OPEN because its constituent AUDIT-F2, AUDIT-F6, and AUDIT-F7 are each STILL_OPEN (see below), even though AUDIT-F1 and AUDIT-F3 are CERTIFIED_CLOSED.

blockerDispositions.title: Architecture Invariant #35 / sourceLedgerEntryId scope mismatch
blockerDispositions.summary: Full-codebase mechanical scan (not a one-off grep) reconfirms zero live DebtEvent creation sites. Roadmap independently re-read and reconfirmed. Part A's four new models introduce no new field/relation to Facility/DebtEvent/LedgerEntry.

auditFindingDispositions.title: Trusted semantic IR not durably persisted
auditFindingDispositions.summary: Reconfirmed against real Postgres with a materially harder nested-tree fixture; tenant isolation verified at the migration-SQL level; content-hash version-bump gating precise at three-level nesting depth. Disclosed non-blocking caveat: no live production code path outside this module's own tests currently reads SemanticTruthRecord yet - the trust-gating read function is correctly implemented, just not yet consumed.

auditFindingDispositions.title: AnalysisRun concurrency claim is racy
auditFindingDispositions.summary: The core atomic claim-time CAS is genuinely correct and held under a 20-way race and a genuinely-concurrent 15-caller race for the same stale row; a stale row can never get permanently stuck. But a real, previously-undisclosed 'zombie writer' risk was found and reproduced: reclaiming a stale RUNNING row has no fencing/lease-token protection, so a presumed-dead-but-actually-slow prior owner can still call completeAnalysisRun/failAnalysisRun/setAnalysisRunStage with the same bare runId and silently overwrite the new owner's live state - the exact class of uncoordinated double-write this fix claims to have eliminated, reappearing via the reclaim path.

auditFindingDispositions.title: Partial instrument failure can disappear
auditFindingDispositions.summary: Re-tested with a deliberately different injection point (mocked runSemanticCoverageAudit instead of Workstream H's own persistSemanticTruthForInstrument) and fresh fixtures. Partial success genuinely preserved; AnalysisRun.status reads PARTIAL; total-failure case durably records every instrument's own failure, not just the first. Generalizes.

auditFindingDispositions.title: BLOCKER-8 only partially remediated
auditFindingDispositions.summary: Same finding as BLOCKER-8 - the N=3 fused-claim recursion gap in findCoordinateClauseSplit.

auditFindingDispositions.title: Live product-flow inevitability unverified
auditFindingDispositions.summary: The confirmed bypass from Part A (upload -> unconditional 'Continue to Review' link with no gate) is still fully reachable - traced directly in documents/page.tsx/actions.ts/review/page.tsx, both functionally and by static source-trace. The new 'Contract analysis' status card does genuinely read real AnalysisRun/AnalysisRunIssue/AnalysisFailureLog state (not a placeholder), but its own 'view findings' link points to the review page, whose entire data layer (lib/onboarding/review.ts) has zero knowledge of ClaimReviewItem - proven by inserting a real ClaimReviewItem row and confirming it is invisible there.

auditFindingDispositions.title: Pre-ownership failure can be log-only
auditFindingDispositions.summary: Both documented failure branches (including the updateMany reclaim-path branch, tested for the first time) are durable, and zero bare console.* error paths remain in lib/contract-model/analysis/**. But a genuine, previously-undisclosed gap cheaper than the disclosed 'total Postgres outage' residual was found: the fix's own recordAnalysisFailureLog call inside the pre-identity catch block has no try/catch of its own - a single failed write there (DB otherwise fully healthy) causes runContractAnalysis to throw uncaught and lose the original failure with zero durable trace, reproducing exactly the log-only failure mode the fix was meant to eliminate.

crossCuttingDispositions.summary: Independent re-derivation (direct production-function calls + real Postgres query, not trusting any script's own tally) confirmed FWRG=0, LSB=0. For DSGR, discovered Part A's own '215' figure is a measurement artifact of the regression script's own tally (excludes ALREADY_RECORDED outcomes), not 215 genuinely-missing review items - a direct DB query found 0 actually missing. A stronger, not weaker, safety result; the script's own metric should be fixed in a future phase, non-blocking here.
Manually traced 3 of 14 historical controls through the real frozen matcher; confirmed zero per-claim branching, NO_CREDIT falls out mechanically from genuine semantic-dimension conflict evidence.

Forced byte-identical instrumentKey+semanticObjectId collision across two companies for SemanticTruthRecord and AnalysisRunIssue; no cross-tenant leakage. One disclosed non-blocking defense-in-depth note (getAnalysisRunIssues/getSemanticTruthForRun aren't independently companyId-guarded, though every current call site is safe).
prisma migrate status/diff both clean; the one new migration is fully additive (2 new enums, 1 additive ADD VALUE, 3 new tables, zero drops/data loss).
